context_for_next_testing_agent: Root-cause AttributeError->RuntimeError conversion (openrouter_providers._call_deepseek / _call_deepseek_direct) is now unit-verified via mocked httpx client. Three _log/_emit sanitisation sites in cto_projects.py verified by static inspection + import-level tests. failure_signature bookkeeping + error_translator new static rule fully covered. If a future task actually wants a LIVE reproduction of the malformed-response case (not just the mocked unit), it will need a preview-only OpenRouter response injector or a debug-mode env flag — none currently exists.
rca of the issue: openrouter_providers._call_deepseek's message-extraction block ran `msg.get('tool_calls')` and `msg.get('content')` without validating `msg` was a dict. When an OpenRouter free-fallback model (walked to on primary-model 402/429/5xx) returned the non-standard shape {'choices':[{'message':'<bare string>'}]}, `msg.get()` raised AttributeError which the surrounding except clause (KeyError, IndexError, TypeError) did NOT catch, so it propagated as an uncaught exception into the cto_projects.py `_run_task_via_api` / `_run_task_with_git` outer handlers. Those handlers previously did `_log(task_id, f'❌ {str(e)}', 'error')` and `_emit(task_id, f'Failed — {str(e)}', kind='fail')`, streaming the raw Python string via SSE into TaskLiveTape.jsx / LiveTaskPopup.jsx which rendered `s.step` verbatim in the chat bubble. Fix has 3 layers: (1) defensive isinstance(msg, dict) guard converts to controlled TypeError caught upstream, (2) sanitized _log/_emit calls use error_classifier.classify_error(e)['user_message'] (never raw), (3) failure_signature tracks whether the same shape is repeating and surfaces a UI banner for deterministic-code failures where blind Retry is futile.
